Product marketing at Mews is at a turning point. The function has been effective at launching products; what it has not yet built is the strategic layer that comes after launch – the continuous positioning, adoption strategy, and market intelligence that makes each product more valuable over time. This role owns that shift.
The Director of Product Marketing and Market Research is a combined senior leadership role responsible for two things that should never have been separated: how Mews brings products to market, and how Mews understands the market it operates in. You will lead the product marketing team, own the research and customer insights function, and serve as the go-to authority on both disciplines for senior leadership across the business.
Mews operates across property management, fintech and payments, guest experience, and marketplace. The right person for this role knows how to build a coherent positioning story across a complex multi-product portfolio – and how to ground that story in real market intelligence, customer insight, and competitive understanding rather than assumption.

Product marketing strategy
Define and own product marketing strategy across the Mews portfolio – covering positioning, messaging, and go-to-market execution from launch through adoption and ongoing engagement.
Build and govern the global product launch framework so that launches are scalable and repeatable, with clear handoffs between strategy and execution.
Own product adoption and post-launch engagement strategy – moving the function beyond launch execution to continuous market thinking that drives usage, retention, and revenue contribution.
Partner with Product, Sales, RevOps, and Customer Success to ensure product marketing strategy connects to commercial outcomes and is reflected in how the business goes to market.
Own NPS tracking programs and design the measurement framework for product marketing impact, including product attach rates, adoption metrics, and pipeline contribution.
Market research and customer insights
Own the end-to-end market research function: identifying research opportunities, designing methodology, running studies, synthesising findings, and activating insights across the business.
Lead primary and secondary research initiatives that inform strategic, commercial, and product decisions – including competitive analysis, customer behaviour, market sizing, and buyer intelligence.
Build competitive intelligence as a structured, ongoing discipline – not a one-off project. Translate competitive signals into positioning decisions, sales enablement, and product roadmap input.
Serve as the functional authority on what the market is telling Mews, and translate that into insight narratives that influence senior leadership decisions and business strategy.
Work closely with Strategy, Product, RevOps, and Marketing to ensure insights land where decisions get made, not just where they get read.
Team and function leadership
Lead and develop a team of product marketers, setting clear expectations, building capability, and creating a culture of commercial accountability.
Set the operating model for how the team works with AI – determining where AI handles execution tasks and where human judgment is irreplaceable, and building team-level standards accordingly.
Serve as the senior leadership go-to on product marketing and market intelligence – the person any executive can trust for a well-grounded, commercially-connected answer.
Represent product marketing and research in executive forums, contributing to annual planning and portfolio prioritisation decisions.

Professional knowledge and experience
10+ years in B2B SaaS marketing, with the majority of that time in product marketing – not demand generation, not agency, not brand-only roles.
Has held a Director, Senior Director, or Head of Product Marketing title, or a broader marketing leadership title that included ownership of the product marketing function.
Proven track record managing and developing a multi-person product marketing team, including hiring, coaching, and performance management.
Experience owning or significantly contributing to a market research or customer insights function – primary research methodology, competitive intelligence programs, or voice-of-customer work.
Deep understanding of B2B SaaS go-to-market strategy: positioning, messaging architecture, pricing and packaging alignment, sales enablement, and lifecycle marketing.
Experience building or significantly reshaping a product marketing function – not just managing an inherited one.
Has operated in a lean, fast-moving environment such as a scale-up, growth-stage, or pre-IPO company. Experience only in large enterprise environments with unlimited resources is unlikely to be a strong fit.

Owns GTM strategy end-to-end – from initial positioning through post-launch adoption and continuous market engagement. Experience limited to launch execution is not sufficient.
Connects product marketing directly to revenue outcomes. Can articulate how their work has influenced pipeline, product attach rates, adoption, or retention – not just campaign outputs.
Translates research into business decisions – not just insight reports. Has a track record of research that changed a strategic or commercial direction.
Multi-functional marketing experience beyond product marketing, for example content, SEO, digital, demand generation, or go-to-market strategy.
Metrics-driven. Comfortable defining and owning the measurement framework for both product marketing impact and research quality.
Strong senior stakeholder communication. Able to influence executive decisions, present with authority, and earn trust through substance rather than seniority alone.
Publicly visible in the product marketing or insights community – speaker, writer, or recognised contributor to the discipline. Not a requirement, but a meaningful differentiator.
AI fluency
AI is changing the product marketing function in a way that is more structural than any other recent technology shift. A significant part of this role is deciding what that means for the team at Mews – what AI handles, what stays human, and how to build a team that operates at a higher strategic level as execution work is automated.

About Spotfire
Spotfire, a business unit of Cloud Software Group , is a leading visual data science and industrial analytics platform designed for complex, high-stakes operational environments.Spotfire combines interactive visualization, data wrangling, advanced analytics, and AI into a single environment—empowering engineers, scientists, and business leaders to solve complex, industry-specific challenges at scale.From energy and high-tech manufacturing to life sciences and financial services, Spotfire delivers the decision-making precision that enterprise organizations rely on to turn data into confident action.

You will join a dynamic, cross-functional team of marketers driving global growth and market adoption. We operate in close partnership with Product, Sales, and Industry GTM to position Spotfire as a tailored, essential solution for solving complex business problems. Our culture values clear communication, rapid execution, and a high standard of operational excellence—we take pride in representing the brand on the ground and turning event interactions into measurable revenue pipeline.

Onsite & Digital Event Execution
Onsite Event Execution: Assist with onsite operations at trade shows, regional events, and meetups, including booth setup, vendor coordination, materials packing/shipping, and staff support.
Digital Event Support: Help manage logistics for virtual events and webinars (setting up event links, tracking registrations, running backend support during live broadcasts).
Lead Capture Setup: Prepare and assist with onsite lead-capture tools (badge scanners, digital forms, check-in apps) to ensure seamless attendee registration and data collection.
Event Promotion & Social Media Outreach
Pre-Event Promotion: Coordinate promotional campaigns to drive attendance, including drafting social media copy (LinkedIn, X), organizing email invite lists, and distributing promotional toolkits to attending sales reps.
Social Media Amplification: Execute event-related social media posts—including live-tweeting/posting from events, capturing photos/videos on-site, and highlighting key speakers or sessions.
Community Engagement: Monitor and respond to event-related social tags, hashtags, and attendee engagement across corporate channels.
Sales Alignment & Lead Operations​
Lead List Processing: Clean, format, and prepare attendee lists immediately following events for prompt CRM upload.
Routing & CRM Assistance: Work within HubSpot to ensure event leads are correctly assigned and routed to the appropriate sales representatives.
Sales Follow-Up Support: Work directly with sales reps and sales managers to monitor lead status, send reminder nudges, and ensure all leads receive proper and timely outreach.
Reporting Assistance: Help gather event metrics, social engagement rates, lead volume, and follow-up data to track overall campaign performance and ROI.

Education: Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Communications, Business Administration, or relevant technical/industry fields (such as Engineering, Energy, Manufacturing, or Data Analytics).
Experience: 3-5 years of experience in marketing support, event coordination, social media management, or sales operations (preferably in B2B SaaS or enterprise technology).
Social & Digital Tools: Hands-on experience managing professional social media platforms (LinkedIn, X) and social scheduling management tools.
CRM & Data Intelligence Tools: Hands-on experience with HubSpot is required; working knowledge or familiarity with ZoomInfo (or similar prospecting/data enrichment platforms) is a strong plus.
Virtual Event Tech: Familiarity with virtual event and webinar platforms (e.g., Zoom Webinars).
Data Proficiency: Comfortable working with Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets (cleaning data, formatting lists, using basic formulas).
Travel: Willingness to travel up to 20–30% to assist with onsite event execution.
Attributes: High attention to detail, strong organizational skills, creative copyediting skills, proactive attitude, and clear written communication.
What Success Looks Like
Flawless Support: Smooth execution, effective promotion, and seamless logistical support for assigned live and digital events.
Increased Engagement: Measurable growth in pre-event registration and live social media engagement surrounding regional events and trade shows.
Data Accuracy & Speed: Cleaning, enriching, and passing off event lead lists to the sales team within 24–48 hours post-event.
Timely Follow-Up & Accountability: Active alignment with sales reps to ensure 100% of event leads receive prompt follow-up, keeping pipeline opportunities moving forward without falling through the cracks.
Insightful Performance Reporting: Delivery of clear, timely post-event reporting that tracks key success metrics—including lead volume, engagement rates, pipeline influence, and overall event ROI

Data privacy has become one of the most strategic challenges facing modern enterprises — sitting at the intersection of AI governance, data operations, and customer trust. As companies adopt AI at scale, they need new ways to automate privacy and manage risk without slowing innovation. As a Senior Demand Generation Manager, you'll own both halves of the pipeline engine: the campaigns that create demand, and the systems that capture, route, score, and measure it. You'll lead paid media across channels like Google, LinkedIn, and YouTube and drive the event calendar, including trade shows, webinars, and executive roundtables.

You'll shape HubSpot as an architect, not just a user, and build the reporting that tells our leadership team whether any of it worked. This isn't a blank slate: paid channels are already live with an agency in place, the event calendar is established, and HubSpot and attribution already exist.

You're inheriting a functioning engine, with plenty of authority to make it even stronger.
It's a small team with a large surface area, so roughly two thirds of your time goes toward driving demand through campaign strategy, paid media, and events, and the other third goes toward building the systems that make that demand measurable and repeatable through HubSpot architecture, lifecycle programs, and attribution. In this role, one person connects both sides of the engine, creating a much tighter link between what we invest, what we learn, and what ultimately produces pipeline.
You'll have real authority to change what isn't working from day one, and on a team this size, a fix you make on Tuesday can be live by Friday. By the end of the year, you'll be the person leadership trusts for a straight answer on whether campaigns and events are actually working.

Translate GTM priorities, ICP definitions, and quarterly pipeline targets into integrated campaigns across paid, events, and email, then build and ship them yourself.
Own paid media end to end, building, launching, and optimizing campaigns across Google Ads, LinkedIn Campaign Manager, and YouTube while partnering with our agency on execution.
Drive the event calendar, including trade shows, webinars, and executive roundtables, sharpening targeting and follow-through while focusing investment on what delivers results.
Carry a quarterly qualified-pipeline number and defend coverage, quality, and conversion with sales leadership, not just volume.
Architect HubSpot as an owner, managing workflows, lifecycle stages, lead scoring, campaign objects, and the Salesforce sync.
Build and defend the metrics that matter, including CPL, cost per qualified opportunity, event-sourced pipeline, and multi-touch attribution.
Partner with Sales, Product Marketing, and RevOps internally, and agencies, venues, and sponsors externally, to run multiple concurrent campaigns and events without dropping a thread.

A track record of hands-on HubSpot ownership, having personally architected and administered an instance, including workflows, lifecycle, scoring, campaigns, and the Salesforce sync.
Direct paid media execution, with hands-on experience building, optimizing, and pacing campaigns in Google Ads and LinkedIn Campaign Manager, not just briefing an agency.
Salesforce fluency, with the ability to navigate objects, fields, and reports and reason about how marketing data lands in the CRM and why it breaks.
B2B SaaS demand generation experience, ideally within a considered, multi-stakeholder sales cycle.
Experience owning event strategy and execution, including trade shows, webinars, and executive-level programs like roundtables or dinners.
Comfort owning a function end to end, balancing strategy with hands-on execution in an individual contributor role.
Strong written and verbal communication, with the ability to effectively manage internal stakeholders and external vendors and partners.

Experience in privacy, data governance, security, compliance, or another regulated, technical software category.
Marketo or Pardot experience alongside HubSpot.
Familiarity with account-based marketing or intent-data tools.
Comfort using AI to speed up operational work, such as campaign QA, data hygiene, or reporting synthesis.
Experience being the first or founding owner of a demand gen or marketing ops function, from the ground up with hands-on responsibility for building and scaling it.
What Success Looks Like

Learn DataGrail's product, buyer personas, and ICP quickly enough to start contributing, not just observing, and meet the marketing, sales, RevOps, and customer success teams to understand what's running and where the friction is.
Take full ownership of the paid channels and the agency relationship, and identify specific over- or under-spending by channel.
Drive the event calendar and process, and produce a keep, fix, or cut recommendation for each program.
Audit HubSpot and existing reporting, and deliver a written list of what's fragile, missing, or misleading in current attribution and lifecycle reporting.
Ship at least one visible fix to a live, underperforming channel or process

Show measurable improvement, with before and after comparisons, on two to three of the biggest inefficiencies identified in the 90-day audit, whether that's rebalanced paid spend, improved event-to-pipeline conversion, or cleaner attribution.
Run paid media and events with full autonomy, proposing and executing budget and calendar changes without waiting on sign-off.
Ship at least three new or rebuilt nurture and re-engagement tracks, with early performance data on each.
Rebuild or upgrade the dashboards used for weekly pipeline calls.
Build a working rhythm with Sales, RevOps, and Product Marketing so hand-offs, routing, and lead flow don't require chasing people down.

Own a program for paid media, events, and HubSpot that runs noticeably better than the one you inherited, with clear before and after numbers on channel efficiency and cost per qualified opportunity.
Be the person others trust when they want to know how well our campaigns and events are actually performing.
Have made real budget and channel calls, moving spend into what works and cutting what doesn't, with pipeline impact you can point to.
Have built a foundation that doesn't need rebuilding when volume doubles.
Have identified where the team needs more support, whether that's tooling, headcount, or an agency change, and made the case for it.

We created Upside to transform brick-and-mortar commerce. Our technology uses the sophistication of online retail—profit measurement, attribution, and incrementality—to provide users with more value on their everyday purchases and brick-and-mortar businesses with new, profitable customers.

We’ve helped millions of users earn 2 to 3 times more cashback than any other product, and hundreds of thousands of brick-and-mortar businesses earn measurable profit.

Billions of dollars in commerce run through the Upside platform every year, and that value goes directly back to our retailer partners, the consumers they serve, and important sustainability initiatives.
The impact you'll make
As Upside's Product Marketer focused on Product Commercialization, you will work at the intersection of our Product and Retailer Go-to-market (RGTM) teams to shape how retailers think about our product. Internally, your work will drive cohesion and clarity across teams. Externally, your work will drive both product adoption and top-line revenue growth by acting as the voice of the retailer during product development, and by leading the commercialization of products and feature releases.

Champion the voice of the retailer , using market and competitive research to highlight opportunities in the product strategy.
Ensure internal alignment by acting as the primary liaison between the Product and Retailer Go to Market (RGTM) teams, to champion the voice of the retailer and align on roadmap priorities
Define our internal product GTM hierarchy in order to ensure effective and impactful launches and positive retailer reception
Contribute to our pricing strategy so that our price point reflects the product's value, covers costs, and meets retailers’ expectations
Drive adoption of new products and features among target prospects, channel partners, and the existing Upside retailer partners
Help to discover and document new product use-cases based on retailer pain points that could turn into new solutions and product offerings
Partner with Revenue Enablement to ensure the Sales and Accounts teams are equipped to tell the product story and accelerate conversion and expansion opportunities

7+ years of experience in product marketing, sales enablement, or a related role —preferably in B2B, SaaS, or a high-growth tech environment. Experience with marketplaces is a plus.
A proven understanding of product commercialization and experience developing strategies to drive product adoption
Outstanding messaging and positioning skills, with the ability to distill complex ideas into clear, compelling value propositions.
Proven track record of crafting high-impact sales enablement content —including pitch decks, playbooks, and competitive battle cards.
Experience working cross-functionally with sales, marketing, and product teams to align on go-to-market strategies.
Demonstrates leadership through influence, earning trust through clear communication, concrete business cases, and compelling storytelling that achieve positive outcomes.
Data-driven approach, with experience using insights to optimize sales performance and messaging.
A bias for action and results, with the ability to work independently and drive initiatives forward in a fast-paced environment.
A genuine passion for problem-solving and applying an analytical approach to each new challenge.
Resiliency, by adopting the evolving nature of the position with a willingness to take on new responsibilities as the role continues to develop and expand.

Track performance metrics across initiatives and provide concise insights and recommendations

This is a rare early-career seat with real surface area. ServiceNow's ISV and Build ecosystem is where partners build products on top of our platform, and this role runs the marketing engine behind them: campaigns, launches, content, and the partner-facing toolkit that hundreds of ISVs use to bring their solutions to market with us. You will not be shadowing someone else's work. You will own programs end-to-end, with a clear line of sight to the pipeline they generate.
You will sit on a global team covering every partner, every region, and every product, which means you will learn the full go-to-market motion faster here than almost anywhere else in marketing. Run demand generation programs with and through ISV partners: digital campaigns, content syndication, webinars, and joint events, including managing the MDF (market development funds) budget behind them
Own the marketing toolkit ISVs use to co-market with us, keeping Campaign Creator assets, playbooks, and enablement content current and actually usable
Support launch marketing for new ISV apps and integrations, from messaging inputs through in-market execution
Build the campaign and asset library that helps partners tell a joint story with ServiceNow
Track and report program performance: what ran, what it cost, what pipeline it produced, and what you would change next time
Activate ISVs who are not yet marketing with us, taking them through onboarding into the program
Manage Partner day to day with product marketing, partner managers, and regional marketing counterparts to keep programs aligned to what the field needs
Align co-marketing campaign roadmaps with product launches, regional priorities, and partner readiness through regular syncs with product marketing, regional teams, and the partner sales org
How you will grow
You will get direct exposure to senior leaders across marketing and the partner organization, hands-on ownership of budget and program outcomes, and a view of the full ServiceNow go-to-market motion. People who do this job well move into named-partner ownership, broader route-to-market roles, and/or deeper specialization in demand generation.

Social-first collaboration is a growing and exciting part of the remit. If it is not yet your strength, we will help you build it.

s.h: Here are some of the EXCITING things you’ll get to do
s.t:
Strategy & Planning

· Lead the Pureplay vertical against ambitious growth targets, owning the number and advising the business on how that growth will be unlocked across retail media and trade marketing.

· Lead Retail Media and Trade Marketing strategy and planning for the vertical across the full marketing funnel: setting the standard for what good looks like, guiding your team’s planning, calendar and prioritisation, aligning UKI execution with global objectives, and deploying investment where it drives the strongest commercial return.

· Be the senior, retailer-facing marketing lead for the vertical, building and progressively deepening relationships with the senior marketing contacts within your retailers, and using them to shape joint plans, unlock opportunities and position SharkNinja as a priority partner.

· Act as the sense-check on the viability of what the Strategy, Sales & Analytics (SSnA) and Sales teams propose: probing, collaborating and keeping a helicopter view to ensure full-funnel plans (including promotional and launch events across the year) are joined up, deliver the commercial volume objectives set by SSnA, align to the SKUs and volumes secured by Sales, and keep marketing investment where it needs to be. Develop and own the digital-channel Joint Business Plans with Sales.

· Align plans with the Brand Media and Integrated Marketing Communications (IMC) teams to maximise the efficiency and impact of total marketing investment, working with them to adjust plans where necessary due to commercial or operational blocks.

· Champion data- and AI-driven commercial planning to sharpen investment decisions, forecasting and prioritisation.
Commercial, Social & Growth

· Bring a commercial lens to everything the team does, spotting opportunities and gaps, developing retailer campaigns and propositions that turn existing and incremental marketing budget into substantial uplifts in product orders and strong return on investment, and partnering and leading with your Sales counterparts (including the Senior Sales Director, Pureplay) and retailers on these conversations.

· Champion social-first collaborations with our retail partners (influencer, organic social and affiliate), amplified through wider full funnel (on and offsite) retailer-owned media activations to build reach, engagement and conversion.

· Own the digital shelf and content excellence agenda (PDPs, brand stores, search and content) and ensure flawless GTM and NPD support, with assets, listings and launch readiness delivered in time and aligned to launch dates.

· Lead the vertical’s presence at selected physical retailer events, partnering with Retail Excellence (Field & Branded Display) and agencies to deliver brand experiences that add commercial value.
Budget & Performance

· Own your vertical’s multi-million-pound marketing budgets, both contracted A&P (Co-op) and any incremental budget secured, ensuring your team plans and deploys them effectively and adjusting at pace to maximise every pound.

· Set the standard for measurement and reporting, ensuring your team reports spend and performance accurately and on time each week to the Head of Retail Marketing and the wider UKI Leadership team, where it feeds into regional and global visibility.
Leadership & Collaboration

· Lead, motivate and support your team (two Trade Marketing Managers and two Retail Marketing Executives across the five pureplay channels, plus a dotted-line Manager), leading from a place of empathy, owning individual development plans, setting clear objectives and building an unstoppable team.

· Work closely with the other vertical leads, and partner end-to-end with Sales, Brand/Category Marketing, SSnA, Studio, Brand Media, IMC and Retail Excellence (Field & Branded Display) to deliver joined-up, best-in-class activation.

· Act as the bridge between local execution and global strategy, connecting UKI pureplay activity to global brand media workstreams and representing UKI in cross-market and EMEA forums.

· Embody the SharkNinja Outrageously Extraordinary mindset and values, living our leadership principles (including ‘winning is a team sport’), comfortable with ambiguity, energised by rewriting the rule book, and bringing retailers, agencies and colleagues on the journey with you.

· Strong commercial acumen and aptitude with the ability to bring a commercial lens to everything the team does, see the opportunities and the gaps, and partner and lead confidently with Sales counterparts and retailers on commercial conversations.

· Experience in retail, trade or channel marketing, ideally within pureplay, e-commerce or marketplace environments (consumer electronics, FMCG or durable goods a plus).

· Proven brand-side experience, having worked in-house for a brand or manufacturer. Retailer and/or agency background alongside this is welcome and valuable.

· A strong working understanding of full-funnel retail media planning and the digital shelf to enable leading a team of specialists, define what good looks like and challenge the plans guiding where adaptions are needed.

· Proven people-leadership experience: managing, coaching and developing a team with empathy, including building individual development plans that grow your people.
Before jumping into all the information about the role and what you can bring to the table, let us introduce ourselves real quick.

Insider One is the #1 platform that brings everything marketing and customer engagement teams need in one place so they can reach their peak potential and become unstoppable.
Our story began with six desks and a vision to create a single platform to make industry-first technologies and emerging channels accessible to marketers worldwide. Today, Insider One is powered by 1,500+ team members representing 50+ nationalities across 30+ offices .

With AI at its core and an integrated Customer Data Platform (CDP), Insider One unites data, personalization, and journey orchestration across the most extensive set of natively supported channels , including WhatsApp, SMS, Email, Web, App, and Site Search.
We recently raised one of the largest funding rounds in the industry, a $500M Series E led by General Atlantic . We are backed by top-notch investors, including Sequoia Capital, QIA, Riverwood, and Endeavor Catalyst , and trusted by 2000+ customers from high-growth startups to the most prestigious Fortune 500 companies such as Samsung, Nike, L’Oreal, Singapore Airlines, Nestlé, Nissan, Lenovo, Puma, IKEA, Allianz, Domino's, and the list goes on.
Insider One was congratulated for becoming one of the only woman-founded, women-led B2B SaaS unicorns in the world. Loved by customers, recognized by analysts, we are the only vendor recognized as the #1 leader in all the capabilities marketing and customer engagement teams need. Don’t just take our word for it — see for yourself . We consistently outperform and continue our leadership, and the results speak for themselves .
From day one, Insider One’s mission has not only been to build a world-class product company, but also to create one of the most socially progressive technology communities in the world.

Through our social responsibility initiatives like 100 Social Responsibility Projects, AI Training for Teachers, Code Academy, SheCodes, SheLeads, and SheMarkables , our community has committed to scaling its impact on our communities across 30+ countries, driving initiatives in health, education, farming, animal rights, and increasing women’s representation in STEM.
Behind all these achievements is an exceptionally talented, visionary team of overachievers that moves fast and agile, creating cutting-edge products, and focuses on making an impact. If you want to be a part of this journey, just keep reading.
What this role is about
We are Insider One — the world’s first Integrated Growth Management Platform, loved by marketers crafting experiences for some of the world’s most renowned enterprise brands. We help enterprise clients connect customer data across channels, predict future behavior with AI and deliver truly individual experiences.
We are expanding our marketing presence across 25 countries and are now looking for our Field Marketing Manager, Northern Europe .

If you’re a self-starter with a passion for B2B marketing and are interested in building the market presence of a unicorn SaaS company in one of the largest and most dynamic regions in the world, this could be the role for you.

Join our dynamic marketing team, create your own playground and take our Northern Europe (UK, Benelux, Nordics) marketing strategy to the next level. Read on to discover how it feels to become one of us.
You might be expecting an eye-catching, mesmerising job description full of start-up jargon — after all, we’re a Sequoia and Riverwood-backed company with an awarded woman CEO and a global team that takes diversity very seriously. But what matters most to us is action – we are underdogs who believe in the power of doing.
So, we asked our VPs of Marketing, Regional Marketing Managers, Country Managers and Sales Teams what they expect from our Senior Marketing Manager, Northern Europe — and this is what they told us.

Build and own the marketing strategy and execution for the UK, Benelux & Nordics, working closely with the global marketing team, your local team of marketing specialists, and the local sales team, to increase awareness, drive engagement, generate leads, and support conversion rates.
Manage all local marketing activities: demand generation, ABM, events, customer marketing, web, content, and PR.
Own the event marketing programme calendars, organising both Insider One-led events and external industry events; manage all aspects of the projects, from speaker recruitment to logistics.
Create locally relevant assets to support sales and campaigns — for example, case studies, whitepapers, and guides.
Work closely with sales to measure programme performance and lead quality.
Act as the go-to for your market, providing insight on trends, unmet needs, and opportunities to deliver greater value to clients by extending company offerings.
Identify emerging markets and market shifts whilst staying fully aware of new products and competitive status. Develop and implement fresh sales/marketing initiatives, strategies, and programmes to capture key demographics.
Present marketing, revenue, and realistic forecasts to the management team.
Collaborate with Marketing, Sales Operations, Sales Engineering, and Sales Enablement functions to ensure alignment and success.
Maintain a clean, up-to-date pipeline and forecast accurately – after all, marketing and demand-gen is a balancing act!
What You Will Need
Minimum 4+ years in B2B SaaS marketing, with a proven track record in demand generation, field marketing, and event management.
Strong leadership skills with experience in building and managing teams.
Good knowledge of the digital space.
Experience with marketing automation and CRM tools (for example, HubSpot, Marketo, Eloqua, Pardot, Salesforce).
Excellent oral and written communication skills, with the ability to create and pitch compelling marketing materials; strong creative problem-solving skills.
Extraordinary attention to detail.
Excellent event planning and execution skills.
The ability to maintain a positive attitude and thrive in a fast-moving environment.

Be part of a diverse team that’s as global as it gets — where every voice is heard and 50+ nationalities build together.
Level up with internal trainings covering AI fundamentals, coding, foreign languages, and a wide range of personal development skills.
Feed your curiosity with access to Spotify, LinkedIn Learning, Blinkist, MasterClass, and CloudGuru.
Become a Shareowner through our eligibility-based “ESOP” and own a piece of what you build.
Help build the team you want to work with and enjoy rewarding referral bonuses.
Opportunities to give back to your community through volunteering and purpose-driven social impact projects.
From global retreats to team-building activities, expect year-round events that turn into lifelong memories.
We aren't just hiring for a position; we are hiring for a mission — a mission to build a lasting legacy that will set the benchmark for the most progressive tech companies out there.

About Ramp
Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.
The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.
We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.
The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.
If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

Ramp is looking for a Performance Marketing Manager to own paid acquisition on YouTube, ChatGPT, X, Rideshare, and Reddit, and to find new incremental channels. You'll take early experiments and turn them into measurable programs and build the operating model that makes successful channels part of Ramp's evergreen performance marketing mix.
This is a high-autonomy role. You will evaluate channel opportunities, design tests, launch campaigns, and analyze full-funnel performance. You'll work with Growth, Creative, Data, Finance, and other cross-functional partners to move quickly while maintaining a high bar for measurement & efficiency.
You’ll use AI as a practical part of the job: building systems that speed up research, campaign creation, performance analysis, and day-to-day channel operations.

Own performance on YouTube, ChatGPT, X, Rideshare, and Reddit. Understand how conversion events, value signals, and lookalike audiences work at a technical level and use that to make channels more efficient over time.
Identify, evaluate, and prioritize new performance marketing channels and acquisition opportunities.
Build the path from experiment to evergreen program: prove incremental SQLs and pipeline impact, hit LTV-to-CAC efficiency targets, and document a repeatable operating playbook.
Own channels as they mature. Decide when a program stays with you and when it transitions to a dedicated owner so you can keep finding new ones.
Analyze performance across the full funnel. Turn incomplete or noisy data into a clear call on what to scale, improve, pause, or stop.
Partner with data and engineering to improve tracking, attribution, and reporting, and with Creative on messaging, format, and ad concepts across surfaces, audiences, and channels.
Build AI agents, workflows, and tools that help the team test more ideas and operationalize channels faster.
What You Need
3+ years in a performance / quantitative marketing, growth, or comparable decision-science role, where you’ve owned numbers and shaped meaningful outcomes.
Strong analytical judgment. You can define success metrics, diagnose and isolate performance issues, and make decisions with imperfect information.
You enjoy designing experiments and translating results into a clear call on what to fund, scale, or kill.
You've built AI workflows, automations, or agents to improve marketing execution and you have good judgment about where AI accelerates the work and where human review is necessary.
You move projects from ambiguity to a clear outcome with limited direction and you're detail-oriented in campaign setup, tracking, and measurement.
Nice-to-Haves
B2B experience.
Experience bringing an experimental channel into a scaled program.
Familiarity with attribution, incrementality testing, randomized controlled tests (RCTs), MMM, and marketing measurement.

Every company is racing to deploy AI agents. Few know how they'll govern them.
As AI moves from experimentation to enterprise-wide deployment, trust, security, compliance, and control have become the biggest barriers to adoption.
That's why we built ServiceNow AI Control Tower.
And now you have an opportunity to help define what’s next. ServiceNow is looking for a Director of Product Marketing to own positioning, messaging, and go-to-market execution for AI Control Tower (AICT), one of the most strategic products in our AI portfolio. This is a rare opportunity to shape a category at the intersection of AI, governance, and security.
You'll own narrative, positioning, launches, web presence, content, campaigns, and demand generation for AI Control Tower, partnering across Product, Engineering, Sales, and executive leadership to drive market impact and business growth. Working alongside a high-caliber Product Marketing team, you'll help bring breakthrough innovation to market and turning great ideas into measurable results.
If you love building markets, not just marketing products, this role is for you.

Own launches end-to-end for AI Control Tower, from planning and messaging through execution, working closely with product, comms, and campaigns to make every release land with impact.
Drive web and digital presence, shaping how AICT shows up on servicenow.com and across digital properties, working with web and creative teams to keep the story sharp, current, and conversion-focused.
Partner on demand gen and digital campaigns with campaign and field marketing to build and optimize programs that generate real pipeline, using messaging and content that make AICT impossible to ignore.
Create the content engine with briefs, web copy, launch assets, sales enablement, campaign content that fuels every team touching AICT in market.
Translate a technical, fast-evolving product into a clear story for governance, security, and IT leaders. You don't need to be an engineer, but you need to genuinely get the AI governance/security space and be excited to go deeper into it.
Work closely with VP+ stakeholders across Product, Engineering, and to make sure launches, campaigns, and content are always grounded in where the product and the market are actually heading.
Bring AI into how you work. Use AI tools strategically in your own day-to-day to draft, research, ideate, and produce content, and bring what you learn back to the team so PMM gets faster and sharper as a group.
Be a builder on a builder's team. This is a leadership opportunity to shape not only AI Control Tower product, but also ServiceNow's company positioning as a leader in AI governance and control, with real room to bring in fresh ideas and best practices.

8+ years in product marketing, with strong chops in launches, web, content, and digital/demand gen campaigns for B2B tech.
Real enthusiasm for AI, security, and governance. You read about this stuff for fun, not just for work.
You use AI tools yourself, already, to work smarter and faster, and you're excited to bring that fluency to a team that wants to keep leveling up.
Comfort getting technical enough to talk credibly with product and engineering.
A track record of running with ambiguity and multiple moving pieces without losing the thread or the fun.
Sharp writing and storytelling instincts. You can make a complex product sound clear, human, and exciting.
Experience collaborating with senior stakeholders with confidence, bring clarity and alignment across different perspectives and priorities.
Why This Role
You'll join at one of the most exciting moments in enterprise technology. ServiceNow AI Control Tower sits at the center of the conversation every executive team is having: how to govern, secure, and scale AI responsibly.
This is your chance to help define that conversation.
You'll shape market perception, influence product direction, work closely with senior leaders, and help build a business at the forefront of ServiceNow's AI strategy. Most importantly, you'll do work that has real impact, with a team that loves what it does and pushes each other to be better every day.
If you're energized by building categories, launching innovative products, and helping customers unlock the promise of AI, this role was made for you.

Senior Technical Product Marketing Manager, Agent Identity & Auth (EMEA)
Location: EMEA

As enterprises move from AI experiments to production agentic systems, a new problem has emerged: agents are non-human actors that need identity, authentication, and authorization — and the traditional identity stack wasn't built for them.
This role owns Kong's story in one of the most important emerging categories in AI infrastructure. As Senior Technical PMM for Agent Identity & Auth, you'll define how the market understands agent identity: how agents are authenticated, what they're authorized to access, and how enterprises establish trust and accountability across autonomous systems.
This is a category-shaping role. You'll build the narrative for a market that's still being defined, with the opportunity to establish Kong as the definitive voice on non-human identity in agentic architectures.

Own positioning and messaging for agent identity and auth — Define the technical narrative for how Kong authenticates, authorizes, and governs agents and other non-human actors across AI and API traffic.
Shape the category — Develop thought leadership that frames the agent identity problem for the market and establishes Kong's point of view through blogs, talks, analyst conversations, and industry engagement.
Lead technical field enablement — Own enablement in this domain for Kong Solution Engineers, Customer Success Managers, and other technical field roles.
Produce deep technical content — Build demos, reference architectures, technical whitepapers, and documentation-adjacent content that helps architects and security teams evaluate and adopt Kong's approach.
Support strategic deals — Serve as the subject-matter expert for sales conversations where agent identity and security are strategic decision criteria, particularly with security and platform engineering buyers.
Fuel launches and campaigns — Deliver technical positioning, proof points, and demo assets as structured inputs to the AI PMM's launch and campaign motions.
Partner with product management — Inform roadmap framing and capability naming based on market feedback, competitive dynamics, and buyer research.

5+ years of experience in product marketing, product management, or solutions engineering -ideally at an Identity and Access Management (IAM) and/or AI Security company.
A genuine, hands-on interest in AI infrastructure. You follow developments in LLM deployment, agentic frameworks, the Model Context Protocol, and AI governance, and can speak credibly to AI platform engineers without bluffing.
A proven ability to translate complex technical concepts into crisp narratives that land with both technical practitioners and C-suite buyers.
Highly collaborative -you thrive working across Product, Marketing, Sales, and Partner teams.
Comfortable owning a stage: keynote presentations, analyst briefings, customer roundtables, and demo-heavy sessions energize you rather than intimidate you.
Experience in open-source software, SaaS platforms, and enterprise go-to-market motions is strongly preferred.
Familiarity with the AI connectivity landscape -including awareness of competing and complementary vendors across API gateways, AI observability, vector databases, iPaaS, and agentic orchestration frameworks - is a strong plus.

Kong Inc., the AI Connectivity Company, is building the connectivity layer of AI. Trusted by the Fortune 500® and AI-native startups alike, Kong’s unified API and AI platform enables organizations to secure, manage, accelerate, govern, and monetize the flow of intelligence across APIs and AI traffic — on any model, any cloud. For more information, visit www.konghq.com .

Marketing Manager
Remote, South Africa. Full-time, permanent, UK hours. R30,000 per month.
Read this before you apply
This is a senior seat at a company of four people. Nobody will train you and nobody has time to check your work. If you need a manager to break tasks down for you, this is not the job. If you have run the whole marketing channel for a small business and you are good at it, keep reading.
The company
Our client is a London-based AI training and transformation consultancy, a year and a half old, founder-led, growing. They teach leadership teams what AI can actually do for their business, then build it with them: data readiness, workflow analysis, AI literacy training, custom AI agents. Two founders, a small payroll, and a fractional CMO who sets direction.
The job
You run marketing end to end for a small, fast-growing business. The fractional CMO owns the strategy, the calendar and the priorities. Everything downstream of that is yours: you take the brief and you deliver it, properly, without being chased and without being taught.
You will be across all of it, social, content, email, events, analytics, paid. But we are not looking for someone who is average at everything. We want you to be genuinely strong in one or two areas and competent across the rest.
What you will actually do
Take a brief from the fractional CMO and execute it end to end, first time, to a standard nobody has to correct
Build and ship email campaigns and automated sequences in ActiveCampaign, including event follow-up flows segmented by who attended and who did not
Own the content and publishing calendar across LinkedIn, Facebook and Instagram
Write. Short-form copy, campaign emails, social, show notes. You will not have a copywriter sitting next to you
Run the SEO programme: what topics the business should own, and the content that wins them
Run and optimise paid campaigns where they earn their place, and report honestly on what they cost and what they returned
Own comms for live events and online workshops, announcement through to post-event follow-up
Keep the tracking honest and produce a monthly report that tells the founders what moved and why
Use AI properly in daily production, not as a novelty
What you need
You have owned marketing end to end at a small business, a startup, or directly for founders. Not a slice of a large corporate marketing department. If your best work was one channel inside a big company, this will not suit you and we would rather say so now
Real depth in one or two areas. SEO and content, or Meta and paid social, or email and lifecycle, or analytics and attribution. Be excellent at something
Numbers you can defend. Not "improved engagement". What was it before, what was it after, what did the business get, and how do you know. You will be asked to walk through a campaign in detail, including what it cost per lead and why that figure is credible
Technical by instinct. You pick up new tools quickly, you have built things yourself, and you use AI because you understand what it can do, not because it is fashionable
You deliver alone. Remote, lightly managed, off a written brief, on time
Experienced enough to have been there and done it. This is not a first or second marketing job

ActiveCampaign specifically, though any serious automation platform transfers
Event marketing
Podcast or video production
Experience marketing a B2B service to business leaders
Two things we will ask you directly
What else are you contracted to do? This is a full-time role and it has to be your only one. We ask everybody, and we ask it first.
Walk me through a campaign you ran, with the numbers. Three of them, with the starting point as well as the finish. If you cannot do that from memory, do not apply yet.
What you get
Full ownership of marketing delivery at a company selling the thing every business is currently trying to work out, with a fractional CMO who knows what he wants and tells you clearly. Full-time, permanent, UK hours, paid in rands into a South African account. Employed through Remote Recruitment , working as part of the client's team.
Equipment
Reliable laptop, stable fibre, quiet professional home working setup.
Process
A recorded screening interview with us, then a task and a final conversation with the founder and the fractional CMO. You will hear back within 24 hours of every stage.

DIRECTV is seeking a Director, Product Marketing – Pricing to lead pricing strategy, planning, and execution across the residential video portfolio. This newly created role will serve as the primary owner of DIRECTV ’s pricing architecture and one of the company’s largest and most sensitive revenue levers.
The Director will lead a team of three pricing professionals and oversee annual price increases, acquisition and rack-rate pricing, customer promotional roll-offs, new package pricing, ancillary fees, and other changes that affect the customer’s bill. The role will also establish consistent business-case standards and pricing governance to ensure decisions appropriately balance revenue, margin, acquisition, churn, and long-term customer value.
This leader will work closely with the Packaging, Offers and Lifecycle teams, as well as Finance, Product, Marketing, Content, Technology, Care, Sales, Legal, and Customer Communications. The Director will operate with significant autonomy, translating enterprise objectives into a 6–12-month pricing roadmap and leading complex initiatives from strategic evaluation through implementation and performance measurement.

Annual and In-Year Price Management (30%)
Lead the strategy, modeling, recommendation, and execution of DIRECTV ’s annual base price increase and acquisition price increase.
Develop recommendations for timing, magnitude, sequencing, and customer allocation of price changes.
Direct in-year pricing actions across the portfolio, including changes to SVODs, premium services, sports products, hardware, regional sports fees, broadcast-related charges, administrative fees, and other bill components.
Maintain an integrated roadmap of planned customer bill changes to identify overlapping events, cumulative customer impacts, operational dependencies, and churn risks.
Coordinate execution across Finance, Technology, Billing, Product, Marketing, Care, Sales, Legal, and Customer Communications.
Identify and manage pricing impacts associated with customer migrations, price guarantees, reconnect and winback programs, legacy billing platforms, and other operational dependencies.
Track pricing realization against the approved business case and recommend corrective actions when results differ from plan.
Pricing Architecture and New Package Pricing (20%)
Own the structural integrity of the pricing ladder across Signature packages, Genre Packs, add-ons, premium services, hardware, and other portfolio components in coordination with offers team.
Evaluate and recommend pricing for new packages, products, features, and services.
Partner with the Packaging team to determine how proposed content or product changes affect package economics, price points, step-up relationships, and customer value.
Maintain clear relationships between acquisition prices, promotional prices, roll-off amounts, and ongoing rack rates.
Assess pricing opportunities and other approaches that better align customer pricing with underlying content costs and market conditions.
Monitor competitive pricing, promotional constructs, package composition, and perceived value across traditional pay-TV providers, virtual MVPDs, and direct-to-consumer streaming services.
Pricing Construct and Roll-off Management (20%)
Continuously evaluate which pricing construct best serves the business — including everyday pricing versus roll-off models.
Analyze elasticity, roll-off behavior, and margin impact to inform construct recommendations.
Treat construct evaluation as an ongoing strategic function rather than a periodic review.
Enterprise Revenue Levers and Business Cases (20%)
Build and oversee financial models and business cases for major pricing, packaging, fee, discount, and revenue initiatives.
Establish consistent assumptions, methodologies, and decision criteria for evaluating revenue, margin, churn, acquisition, migration, and customer lifetime value.
Develop scenarios and sensitivities that make key assumptions, risks, and tradeoffs clear to executive decision-makers.
Evaluate pricing for regional sports, broadcast programming, hardware, premiums, SVODs, bolt-ons, and other significant revenue or cost-recovery levers.
Quantify the direct and downstream effects of pricing decisions on gross additions, ACPU, retention, package mix, migration, and long-term profitability.
Partner with Finance to ensure business cases align with forecasts, budgets, content economics, and enterprise financial objectives.
Conduct post-launch measurement to compare actual performance with the approved business case and incorporate learnings into future decisions.
Oversee the development of pricing analytics, tools, and capabilities required to support faster and more rigorous decision-making.
Pricing Governance and Cross-Functional Partnership (10%)
Establish clear pricing governance, approval processes, decision rights, and documentation standards.
Serve as the central point of coordination for proposed changes affecting the customer’s recurring or one-time bill.
Partner with the Offers team to ensure acquisition, retention, winback, proactive, and tactical offers fit within the overall pricing architecture and approved economic guardrails.
Partner with the Packaging team to ensure package design, content decisions, and price points work together to create a logical and competitive customer value proposition.
Bring forward fact-based recommendations that clearly articulate financial opportunity, customer impact, execution requirements, and key risks.
Present pricing strategies and recommendations to senior and executive leadership.
Team Leadership
Lead, coach, and develop a team of pricing analysts and specialists.
Establish clear roles, priorities, performance expectations, and development plans for the team.
Create a high standard for analytical accuracy, financial discipline, executive-ready communication, and executional follow-through.
Ensure the team develops a detailed understanding of customer behavior, competitive dynamics, billing platforms, product economics, and operational dependencies.
Build strong partnerships across functions while maintaining clear accountability for pricing recommendations and outcomes.
Foster a culture of curiosity, constructive challenge, ownership, and continuous improvement.

s.h: What you’ll need to be successful
s.t:
Extensive experience in pricing strategy, revenue management, product strategy, or a related discipline, preferably within subscription, telecommunications, media, entertainment, or another recurring-revenue business.
Demonstrated experience leading large-scale price changes from initial strategy and financial modeling through implementation and performance measurement.
Strong understanding of subscription pricing constructs, including introductory pricing, rack rates, promotional guarantees, roll-offs, fees, discounts, and everyday pricing.
Experience evaluating new product or package pricing and managing pricing relationships across a multi-product portfolio.
Advanced financial modeling and business-case development skills, with a strong understanding of revenue, margin, churn, acquisition, customer lifetime value, and P&L impact.

We are looking for a global Product Marketing Manager to drive Fieldwire's growth, with a particular focus on enterprise customers and large general contractors, specialty contractors, and construction owners.
This role sits at the intersection of product, sales, customer success, and marketing. You will develop positioning, messaging, go-to-market strategies, sales enablement, and thought leadership programs that help customers understand how Fieldwire solves real construction challenges.
The ideal candidate brings experience in enterprise SaaS, construction technology, or adjacent industries and has a passion for translating complex technology into compelling customer value.
The primary responsibilities for our next Product Marketing Manager will be to:
Go-to-Market Leadership
Lead global go-to-market strategy and execution for new product launches, feature releases, integrations, and platform initiatives.
Develop messaging, positioning, and value propositions tailored to enterprise construction customers.
Build launch plans that drive awareness, adoption, and revenue growth.
Market Intelligence
Develop deep expertise in the North American construction technology landscape.
Monitor competitive trends and emerging technologies, including AI, BIM, project management, and field productivity solutions.
Conduct customer research, interviews, surveys, and win/loss analysis to uncover market opportunities.
Sales Enablement
Create sales presentations, battlecards, customer-facing assets, and training materials.
Support enterprise sales cycles through customer presentations, webinars, and marketing campaigns.
Equip sales teams with clear messaging and competitive differentiation.
Content & Thought Leadership
Develop compelling content across blogs, webinars, whitepapers, videos, case studies, events, and digital campaigns.
Partner with customers to showcase success stories and measurable business outcomes.
Help position Fieldwire as a trusted voice in construction technology, AI, BIM, and field productivity.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
Partner with Product, Sales, Customer Success, Demand Generation, and Field Marketing teams to align priorities and drive business outcomes.
Act as the voice of the customer across the organization.
At Fieldwire, we’re looking for our next Product Marketing Manager to have the following skills and experiences
3-5+ years of experience in Product Marketing, Product Management, Solutions Marketing, or related roles.

Experience marketing enterprise SaaS products.
Construction technology experience strongly preferred (Field Management, Project Management, BIM, ERP, Scheduling, Document Management, AI, or related solutions).
Demonstrated success launching products and driving adoption in enterprise markets.
Strong executive communication and presentation skills.
Ability to create compelling narratives for technical and business audiences.
Experience supporting enterprise sales organizations.
Comfortable working in a fast-paced, highly collaborative environment.
And if you have any of the following, we REALLY want you to apply today!
Experience working with General Contractors, Specialty Contractors, Owners, or Construction Technology providers.
Familiarity with construction project management platforms.
Experience bringing AI-powered products to market.
Public speaking and industry event experience.

You call. You wait. You call again. In every other part of your life, you book in seconds. In healthcare, you’re blocked.
We’re here to give power to the patient.
For nearly 20 years, we’ve built the leading healthcare marketplace - helping tens of millions of people find and book the care they need. Now, we’re going further: building our infrastructure beyond Zocdoc’s marketplace to power access to care wherever patients search, from provider websites and insurance directories to search engines, AI platforms, and more.
Healthcare still lacks something every other major consumer industry takes for granted: a seamless way to go from seeking to getting . We don’t want to own the front door to care; there isn't one. We want to make sure all of those doors open when patients are knocking.
Fixing healthcare starts with fixing access to it. And we're still just getting started.

As the Director of Patient Product Marketing, you'll be the strategic voice of the patient inside Zocdoc's Product Marketing organization.

Reporting to our VP, Product Marketing, you'll own the overarching positioning, narrative, and GTM strategy for the entire patient-facing portfolio–defining how millions of consumers discover, choose, and come to trust Zocdoc.

In this role, you will lead and scale a high-performing team of PMMs, pairing deep market insights with visionary audience strategies that accelerate customer adoption and long-term business growth. By staying ahead of where healthcare is going, you’ll paint a clear picture of the future for patients while helping to shape our product strategy.

You will lead our PMM team into an AI-native era—championing automated GTM workflows and modern tool stacks that allow the team to scale efficiently and focus on high-impact work.

Owning go-to-market strategy and positioning across our consumer portfolio, serving as strategic partner to design, product, and GMs, and bringing a sharp perspective on the exact consumer segments we should build for
Leading and coaching a team of PMMs, setting the standard for audience strategy, messaging simplicity, and high-impact GTM execution
Informing the product discovery with market context, validating user needs and competitive dynamics to ensure our roadmaps deliver clear patient value and strong product-market fit
Championing the shift toward scalable GTM capabilities and AI-native ways of working to maximize business impact
You'll Enjoy This Role If You...
Love turning complex user behaviors into clear, compelling positioning and GTM strategy
Are energized by building and coaching a team of product marketers
Can speak with equal fluency to a GM about market opportunity and to a product team about patient psychology and user experience
Have an interest in transforming the healthcare experience for millions of patients
Are comfortable being the accountable owner of a narrative that spans multiple products and teams
Take pride in balancing big-picture strategy with the coaching and rigor it takes to bring a team along with you
You'll be successful in this role if you...
Have 12–15+ years of relevant marketing experience, including 8+ years in product marketing and demonstrated success building and leading teams, including people managers
Have deep experience with consumer products or marketplaces, ideally where trust, choice, and repeat engagement drive the business
Have a track record of shaping company-level narrative and positioning, not just individual product launches
Are a systematic coach who uses structured approaches to assess talent, build development plans, and recruit outside talent
Can navigate ambiguity and competing priorities, making sound tradeoffs with incomplete information
Are an exceptional communicator who can translate complex or sensitive topics for senior leaders and represent the function in high-visibility conversations
Have applied external market and industry insight to sharpen positioning and drive performance

Creative problem-solver: Working with the team to market to a new audience and find innovative ways to grow the brand.

You’re happy being accountable for results. You have a track record of achieving ambitious business results, and you’re comfortable being assessed on that basis. You know how to prioritise your work for maximum impact.
You are a self-starter and have a proactive, positive attitude and love turning complex, moving parts into a seamless customer launch experience.
Experience in tech or finance for sole traders or SMBs is a huge plus.

Responsabilidades e atribuições
No seu dia a dia, você terá um papel crucial na gestão do time, do negócio e dos projetos:
Liderança e Mentoria: Realizar conversas individuais de desenvolvimento de carreira e sessões mensais de mentoria , avaliando as necessidades de desenvolvimento e performance dos membros da equipe e garantindo a criação e execução de Planos de Desenvolvimento Individual (PDI);
Gestão de Horas e Projetos: Designar e monitorar tarefas operacionais diárias e ongoing , sendo o ponto de referência para priorização e escalonamento de problemas complexos.
Garantia de Qualidade (QA): Manter a responsabilidade geral pelo QA (Quality Assurance) das execuções de mídia do time , incluindo a revisão de orçamentos, pacing, segmentação e targeting, entre outras.
Estratégia e Arquitetura de Campanhas: Arquitetar campanhas de acordo com as melhores práticas de mercado e necessidades do cliente, definindo a lógica de setup para plataformas in-scope e adjacentes.
Client Management e Relacionamento: Assegurar o sucesso do cliente e o cumprimento dos SLAs , atuando como PoC (Ponto de Contato) principal no dia a dia para construir confiança e rapport.
Crescimento do Negócio: Sinalizar em caso de oportunidades de serviços incrementais e co-liderar conversas, utilizando o conhecimento do negócio do cliente para informar a estratégia.
Participar ativamente de reuniões com clientes e stakeholders-chave, garantindo que as expectativas e necessidades sejam compreendidas e atendidas;
Desenvolver e implementar estratégias eficazes de marketing digital em múltiplos canais, como Google Ads, Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok e programática, otimizando resultados e alinhando com os objetivos do negócio;
Elaborar planos de mídia que maximizem o impacto das campanhas e alcancem os KPIs estabelecidos;
Auxiliar a equipe no monitoramento e execução das campanhas, desde o lançamento até a entrega de relatórios finais, garantindo que as entregas estejam alinhadas às projeções e metas estabelecidas.
Requisitos e qualificações
Para a posição de Coordenação em Mídias de Performance é obrigatório:
Domínio Avançado ou Fluente em Inglês: Essencial para a comunicação eficaz em um ambiente internacional e relacionamento com stakeholders globais;
Expertise em Mídias Digitais de Performance: Experiência sólida na criação, otimização e gestão de campanhas em diversas plataformas de mídia digital, incluindo Google Ads, Meta Ads (Facebook e Instagram), TikTok, Pinterest e Programática;
Gestão e Desenvolvimento de Pessoas: Histórico comprovado de liderança, gestão de equipes e desenvolvimento de talentos, com foco em planos de crescimento individual;
Autonomia e Proatividade : Capacidade de tomar decisões de forma independente, agir com iniciativa e gerenciar cenários complexos com eficácia;
Comprometimento com Prazos e Resultados: Habilidade para gerenciar múltiplas demandas e garantir a entrega de resultados dentro dos prazos estabelecidos, sempre com alto nível de responsabilidade.

s.t:
Asset Living is a third-party management firm and a proven partner in fostering thriving communities nationwide. Founded in 1986, Asset Living has decades of experience delivering exceptional value to our partners.

Since the beginning, our undeniable passion has driven our organic growth from a small property management firm to one of the most trusted allies in real estate.

Asset Living's growing portfolio includes a multitude of properties across the country that span the multifamily, single-family home rentals, affordable housing, build-to-rent, active adult, and student housing divisions.
Asset Living is a fast-growing company made up of talented individuals from diverse backgrounds that differentiate us and help us drive innovation and results for our clients and communities across the US. At Asset Living, we wholeheartedly believe 'Together We Lead, Together We Succeed’.

We empower each other to lead by example, collaborate, and evolve – inspired by our belief that we can continually improve as individuals and as an organization. Together, we create an environment where every voice is heard, every idea is valued, and every individual experiences opportunities to grow as our company grows.

When you join Asset Living, you become part of a dynamic team that thrives on unity, unique talents, and a universal culture of winning.
Recognized as one of the nation's Best and Brightest Places to Work and ranked in the NMHC top 50 professionals, join Asset Living because of its reputation as the most trusted partner in real estate, workplace culture, and growth opportunities.

Asset Living is a member of The Institute of Real Estate Management (IREM) and is recognized as an Accredited Management Organization (AMO). Together, we lead the way, and together, we achieve excellence in all that we do. Join a workplace where success is a collective journey and leadership is a shared responsibility.
Marketing Associate
As the Marketing Associate, you will play a pivotal role in providing unparalleled strategic marketing support and insight to a portfolio of properties, serving both our operational leadership team and our valued clients.

In this role, you will collaborate closely with operational leadership to establish and execute effective marketing efforts and leverage your expertise to develop and implement innovative marketing plans, while continuously analyzing performance data to ensure efficiency and success.

Works closely with operational leadership on maintaining successful property marketing efforts that supports overall leasing efforts of assigned portfolio.
Responsible for leveraging centralized marketing team support, individual expertise, and preferred vendor partner services to develop and execute marketing plans and strategy for assigned portfolio.
Responsible for analyzing ongoing leasing and marketing performance, as well as preparing and providing performance data reporting to operational leadership and clients.
Responsible for recommending and overseeing the execution of long-term and short-term goals with timelines, benchmarks, and KPIs using data to drive decision making and recommendations.
Participates in regularly scheduled calls with operational leadership and clients to review marketing performance of assigned communities.
Provides leasing and marketing training and best practices to onsite teams.
Creates additional marketing ideas and campaigns for prospects, resident referrals, resident events, etc. to increase social media presence and drive qualified traffic to the communities.
Creates 30-60-90-day marketing action plans for properties not meeting occupancy goals.
Travel Requirement: This position may entail travel, estimated at 5% of work time annually for internal meetings.
The candidate must be located in Phoenix, AZ.

Bachelor's degree in marketing, communications, or a related field.
Proven experience in marketing support or a similar role.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Familiarity with online digital marketing platforms.
Excellent organizational skills with the ability to multitask and prioritize effectively.
Creative mindset with a keen eye for detail.
Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively in a team environment.

1-3 years marketing experience that directly supports marketing manager responsibilities; paid digital media, marketing strategy, data-driven decision making.
Experience in Real Estate Property Management
Experience with Property Management Software – Yardi, Onesite, Entrata
Experience with industry-related CRMs – Rent Dynamics, Knock.
